Subject: Residency questions — where do requests run?

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. We need a short Q&A for our security/compliance review focused on three things: (1) which regions/processors handle inference requests, (2) what subprocessors are involved and where they operate, and (3) how Redwood treats cross-border transfers and deletion guarantees (esp. for CCPA/EU export).

Could you provide a one-page summary and any evidence we can include in our vendor assessment? I attached a short spreadsheet with the fields our procurement team wants filled (novex_qna_initial.xlsx).

High-level context: Novex Health will be routing PHI-derived, pseudonymized payloads to the model endpoint. We expect ~500k requests/month initially, mostly US/EU users.

Would appreciate a response by EOD Thursday if possible.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Residency questions — where do requests run?

Hi Elena —

Following up with a more technical breakdown. I grouped responses to match your spreadsheet columns. High level points first, then specifics: 

High-level
- Hosted model endpoints: requests are executed in the region of the chosen endpoint (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1). We also offer Dedicated and Private deployment modes (VPC/on-prem) if you need deterministic locality.
- Smart routing: for hosted customers we route to the nearest available capacity by policy; customers can pin region or model variant to avoid cross-border routing.
- Subprocessors: compute runs on cloud providers (primary: AWS, secondary: GCP for some regions). We use a managed logging/metrics provider for telemetry and a CDN for optional edge caching.

Processing specifics (responses you can paste into your spreadsheet):
1) Where are requests executed?
- Default hosted routing: executed in the customer region selection (we currently have official execution zones in: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1). Requests originating from EU customers can be pinned to eu-west-1.

2) Which subprocessors are involved (and where)?
- Compute: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west4) — see Appendix A attached (appendix_a_subprocessors.csv).
- Storage/KV cache: managed Redis service (region-matched).
- Monitoring & telemetry: third-party provider (US-based, processes aggregated metadata only).
- Key management: customer-managed KMS available (recommended) or Redwood-managed KMS (AWS KMS in selected regions).

3) Cross-border transfers & export controls
- Export profile: Redwood does not intentionally export customer request payloads outside the pinned region for customers who select regional execution. For standard hosted customers without pinning, we may route to other zones in the same cloud region for capacity — e.g., us-west <-> us-east — but not across major legal territories unless you opt-in to multi-region fallbacks.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to other regions only occurs when customer policy allows it; we provide flags in the customer config to disable cross-border fallback entirely.

4) Data retention and deletion
- Inference transient data: request payloads and tokenized context are ephemeral in the runtime; KV cache entries and prefixes may persist for configured TTLs (default 24 hours for cache). We persist minimal telemetry for billing/diagnostics (token counts, latencies) for 90 days by default.
- Deletion SLOs: for hosted customers, we support on-demand dataset erasure requests with confirmation of deletion within 7 business days for data in primary stores; for caches and runtime ephemeral state, deletion is immediate upon TTL expiry or wipe command.
- Legal hold: if a legal hold is required, we can isolate retention and provide a scoped export that prevents automated purging — Kimberly can add more on process.

Evidence available: subprocessor CSV (attached), SOC 2 excerpt, processing flow diagram, and sample deletion confirmation logs (we redact PII for any shared logs).

Clarifying question: are you planning to use the Hosted API (we manage region/pinning) or Redwood Private (VPC) for production? Private gives you full control and simplifies export control compliance.

-TL;DR attachments: appendix_a_subprocessors.csv

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.inference

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A couple follow-ups from procurement/security: 
- We need a committed erasure SLA that says deletion requests for persistent logs/subprocessor stores will be completed within X days. Is 7 business days guaranteed in contract?
- For EU-origin data, we need an assurance that no export to the US occurs without documented legal basis. Will pinning to eu-west-1 and a contractual prohibition on cross-border fallback satisfy this?
- Auditability: we will need a deletion confirmation artifact (timestamped event and hash) and an audit log showing the erase action.

We attached our evidence request template (ccpa_ev_request.docx) — can you confirm which items you can provide as-is and which require an NDA or redaction?

Also, we are evaluating Private (VPC) vs Hosted. If we go Hosted with strict pinning, will Redwood provide the same deletion confirmations?

Best,
Elena

Elena —

Bringing this to a close and proposing concrete next steps so your procurement team has what it needs: 
1) Contract commit: we can include a 7-business-day deletion SLA for persistent stores in our standard MSA for Hosted customers. For Private deployments we offer a 3-business-day SLA as part of the enterprise addendum.
2) EU pinning: pinning to eu-west-1 + explicit contractual prohibition on cross-border fallbacks satisfies standard export constraints; we will scope language for your legal team.
3) Audit artifacts: we will produce a deletion confirmation artifact (timestamp + SHA256 hash of manifest) and an admin audit log extract. These are available for Hosted customers; for live production evidence we can provide redacted samples and a fresh audit extract under NDA.
4) Evidence pack: I'll place the following into the shared Drive folder and can send the full pack once we have an NDA in place: appendix_a_subprocessors.csv, SOC2-excerpt.pdf, processing_flow_diagram.png, sample_deletion_confirmations.txt. I also attached a zipped evidence bundle preview (redwood_evidence_pack_v1.zip).

- Elena/Curtis: confirm NDA workflow so we can push full evidence.
- Novex: confirm whether you prefer Hosted (pinned eu-west-1) or Private (VPC). If Hosted, confirm the non-fallback requirement; we will add clause to deal.
- Markus: set up 30-min call Thursday 10:00 AM PT (pending) and upload the Drive folder.

We aim to have the formal evidence pack available within 48 hours of NDA execution.

Regards,
